summary: Gone Siouxon Peak lookout site in the Gifford Pinchot NF: a 1920s cupola cabin, an L-4 cab from 1935, and summit remnants recorded in 2021.

facts.design: Cupola cabin of the 1920s, replaced in 1935 by an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: No standing structure reported; summit remnants (hook anchor, stovepipe, phone-line pegs, shed pad, privy and garbage pit) recorded on WillhiteWeb in 2021; removal date not recorded, probably 1960s per Oregon Hikers

access.note: Reached on foot by a hike of about 2 miles with 1,500 ft of gain; sources describe a hiking route and name no closure or permit. Level inferred from hiking guides, not from a Forest Service notice

visit.trail_note: About 2 miles and 1,500 ft of gain; the short trail to the lookout is not signed; some access roads need high clearance because of berms

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)

events.note: Cupola cabin probably finished in summer 1921 per WillhiteWeb; FFLOS and Oregon Hikers say the 1920s
Crews pulled out of the Siouxon fire district in August 1927; a newspaper expected the stations to burn and reported instruments removed and houses abandoned
Panorama photographs taken July 31, 1937 show a phone line, flagpole, stovepipe, weather station and shed
Last dated image in the WillhiteWeb record; the date the cab was destroyed is not known
Registered July 17, 2012 as FFLOS US 1341 (WA 241), nominated by Ray Kresek
WillhiteWeb visit photos dated November 20, 2021 record summit remnants

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Oregon Hikers say the 1920s, and the firelookout.com heading lists 1931 to the 1960s. WillhiteWeb dates the cupola to probably summer 1921 from an October 1921 newspaper item. The story gives 1921 as probable and reports the other dates as conflicting.
Oregon Hikers says the tower was probably demolished in the 1960s and FFLOS says the date of the L-4 destruction is unclear. No year is recorded, so no removal event is logged.

notes_for_editor: Gone site; only WillhiteWeb (cite 2) describes the 2021 summit remnants, so the today section rests on one source. The 1921 build year is WillhiteWeb's inference ('probably'); FFLOS and Oregon Hikers say 1920s. County conflict: brief and FFLOS say Lewis County, while the Washington lookouts index (cite 5) files Siouxon Peak under Skamania County. The story does not name a county; please check. Access level 'public' is inferred from hiking guides (cite 3, cite 2), not from a Forest Service notice. No WebSearch result gave a Forest Service closure notice.
